title: Priming gapfield microburst scratch
content:
Scratchpad: priming-gapfield / microburst warmup oscillations
Owner: Claire Bennett (eng-serving-runtime)
Collaborators: Marcus Lee, Asha Nair
Date range: quick runs 2025-01-11 -> 2025-01-18

Background / motivation:
- Observed repetitive small spikes (5–30s) of elevated p99 during mixed short/long traffic that do not align with cold-starts or clear GPU allocation churn.
- Hypothesis: small "priming gapfields" in KV cache + tokenizer prefill interplay cause bursty extra compute on some requests (context re-materialization, suboptimal caching) that ripple into tail latency when arrival clusters hit hot tokens.
- Goal: reproduce in controlled bench, isolate whether warmup is cache-latency, kernel mismatch, or batching artifact.

Environment / config (runs):
- Model: open-architecture 7B variant (quantized int8), KV-enabled, prefilling allowed.
- Server: redwood-inference/runtime v2.8.1 (local dev cluster), single A100-40GB, dockerized serving with 4 worker threads, continuous-batcher enabled.
- Workload generator: custom harness (GH: redwood/repro-priming-gaps) that can emit burst clusters, background low-rate noise, and long-context fillers.
- Key toggles: KV_CACHE_ON {true,false}, PREFILL_STRIP=short/long, BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=2/8/20, TOKENIZER_SHARD=on/off

Micro-experiment matrix (high level):
- A: baseline steady Poisson @ 40 qps (p50 ~ 18ms)
- B: intermittent microburst (60 qps for 10s every 2m) with KV_CACHE_ON=true
- C: same as B but KV_CACHE_ON=false
- D: B with BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS=20 (higher batching latency)
- E: B with PREFILL_STRIP=long (adds large prefill to a subset)

Representative run log (select):
- Run B (KV on), BATCH_TIMEOUT=8, generator: burst 60 qps x10s every 120s, sample histogram over 15m window.
  - qps observed: baseline 40, burst peak 62
  - p50: 21ms, p95: 78ms, p99: 291ms
  - spike pattern: p99 jumped in 3 repetitions, each spike lasting ~12–22s starting 0.6s into the burst window.
  - tail shape: bimodal during bursts (fast path ~<40ms, slow path ~250–350ms).

- Run C (KV off), everything else same:
  - p50: 24ms, p95: 130ms, p99: 510ms
  - observation: overall worse tail, spikes longer and higher amplitude.

- Run D (BATCH_TIMEOUT=20):
  - p50: 26ms, p95: 95ms, p99: 320ms
  - notes: increased batching smoothed some p95 but introduced a secondary longer tail in p99 due to queuing behind large batches.

Quick ASCII timeline (simplified p99 over time for run B):
[time 0m         2m         4m         6m]
p99:   _/\____/\_________/\_____   (peaks align with bursts)
Legend: each \/ denotes a ~10–30s high-tail window

What I instrumented that helped narrow root cause:
- Per-request KV cache hit/miss labels (added logging): saw a ~12% miss rate concentrated at burst start. Misses correlated with requests that also had long prefill lengths (>3k tokens).
- Traced kernel-switch events: when a long prefill request hits, runtime picks a fallback kernel path due to memory patterns; subsequent small requests occasionally queue behind that request and pay the penalty (GPU kernel scheduling + host->device movements).
- Batcher traces: observed batch composition heterogeneity at burst boundary — 1 big prefill + N small requests => single batch dominated by big request.

Interim conclusions:
- Primary amplification vector appears to be mixed-length batching at burst start: presence of a long-prefill request in early batch leads to much longer per-batch latency and drags small requests into the slow path.
- KV cache misses amplify the effect (longer prefill causes cache updates, page-in costs).
- Increasing batch timeout trades p95 improvements for p99 risk because you increase coalescing probability (bad when mixed lengths present).

Actionable hypotheses to test next (prioritized):
1) Enforce batch composition guard: cap per-batch total prefill tokens or reject long-prefill in first 50ms of burst window. Expectation: reduces p99 amplitude.
2) Pre-warm technique: schedule background priming traffic of synthetic long-prefill requests just before predicted bursts (simulated). Check whether KV hit rate increases and p99 reduces.
3) Kernel preselection: if we detect an incoming long prefill, route it to a separate worker pool so it doesn't contaminate mixed batches.
4) Triage: try small clients-only lane (soft priority lanes) to ensure short requests take fastpath even when large requests exist.

Planned microbenchmark to validate (for next run):
- Controlled two-lane experiment: (lane A short-only 40 qps, lane B long-only 2 qps scheduled to coincide) + two worker pools. Compare: p99_short when colocated vs isolated.
- Metrics to record: per-batch token sum, per-request kernel-type, kv-hit bool, batch-size distribution, queue-wait-ms.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are kernel-switch costs dominated by host-GPU mem copies or by different cuBLAS/cuDNN paths? Need CUDA profiling to know.
- Is there an interaction with memory allocator fragmentation on long-lived GPU buffers after repeated long-prefill runs? (allocator traces needed)
- How would multi-tenant Dedicated pools behave (we're on single-tenant dev box now)? Cross-tenant noise could make this worse or hide it.

Quick TODOs (next 7 days):
- [ ] Implement per-batch token cap in the local batcher (Marcus)
- [ ] Add synthetic pre-warm mode to harness and run scheduled priming (Asha)
- [ ] Run CUDA sampling (.nvprof / Nsight-lite) on a failing spike to capture kernel-level timeline (me)
- [ ] Create dashboard widget for "batch-token-sum" and "batch-dominant-request-id" in Console (low priority but helpful)

Notes to self (observational):
- Spikes often begin ~0.6–1.2s after burst start — hints at the timing for a pre-warm window (warm a few hundred ms before expected burst).
- Simple KV-off test made overall tail worse; so caching helps but is not the root cause.
- An ad-hoc mitigation that temporarily reduced p99: if we artificially delay the very first long-request by 200ms (so it misses the first small batch), the rest of that burst had much smaller tail.

Experiment log refs / file attachments:
- GH run artifacts: GH: redwood/repro-priming-gaps/actions/runs/9831 (raw histograms, batch traces)
- Local trace snapshot: /tmp/priming-gap-20250118.tgz (kernel logs + batch traces)

This doc is a working scratchpad — will convert top hypotheses into a small PR that implements per-batch token cap and a two-lane worker routing test once the CUDA profiling yields more signal.

End of scratchpad.
